# Volume 3 — Chapter XXX Mrs. Skinner’s Romance

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Nell disembarked from the train at Coombe Road station and searched the surroundings to check whether somebody had arrived to greet her. She was supposed to lodge with a particular Miss Thora Sweet, yet no individual present matched even slightly the mental image she had built of that woman based on the letter from Esther. The sole human visible was an aged female, seated within a wagon that had mail bags stacked all around her. Estimating her weight at two hundred pounds would have been generous; her countenance was as circular and crimson as a harvest-moon, possessing nearly as few distinct features. She was dressed in a snug, black, cashmere gown, crafted according to the style from a decade prior, a slightly dusty black straw hat ornamented with yellow ribbon bows, and bleached black lace mits.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0000 }

“Over here, you,” she shouted, gesturing toward Nell with her whip. “Is the new Coombe Road schoolma’am you?”
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0001 }

“Yes.”
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0002 }

“Indeed, that was my belief. Attractive schoolma’ams are famous on Coombe Road, in the same way that Millersville is famous for ugly ones. Thora Sweet inquired of me earlier today whether I was able to drive you out here. I replied, ‘Sartin I kin, if she don’t mind being scrunched up some. This rig of mine’s kinder small for the mail bags and I’m some heftier than Thomas!’ Allow me a moment, miss, to move these bags around slightly, and I will fit you in one way or another. Thora’s place is merely two miles away. The hired boy belonging to her next-door neighbor will retrieve your trunk this evening. I am called Skinner—Amelia Skinner.”
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0003 }

Nell was finally nestled into bed, swapping entertained grins with her own reflection as it happened.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0004 }

“Move faster, black mare,” ordered Mrs. Skinner, as her plump hands took hold of the reins. “I have never driven the mail rowte before. Today, Thomas wished to hoe his turnips, which led him to ask that I take his place. Consequently, I simply sat down, grabbed a quick bite while standing, and set off. It pleases me somewhat. Naturally, it proves somewhat tedious. During certain moments I sit and ponder, whereas during others I simply sit. Move faster, black mare. Getting home early is my goal. Being without me makes Thomas extremely lonely. After all, our marriage took place quite recently.”
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0005 }

“Oh!” Nell uttered in a polite tone.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0006 }

“Only one month. Yet Thomas pursued me for a rather long period. The whole thing was truly romantic.” Nell attempted to imagine Mrs. Skinner engaged with romance, but she could not.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0007 }

“Oh?” she uttered once more.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0008 }

“Indeed. You see, a second gentleman pursued me afterwards. Keep moving, dark horse. Having been a widow for such an extended period, people no longer anticipated my remarriage. However, upon the departure of my daughter—a schoolteacher like yourself—to the West for a teaching job, I experienced true loneliness and was not at all opposed to the prospect. In due course, Thomas started calling on me, as did that other man—William Obadiah Seaman was what he was called. A lengthy duration passed during which I was unable to decide which one to choose, while they continued to visit repeatedly, and my anxiety persisted. You see, W.O. possessed wealth—his property was splendid, and he maintained quite a grand manner. He was easily the superior prospect. Keep moving, dark horse.”
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0009 }

“What stopped you from marrying him?” inquired Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0010 }

“Indeed, you see, I wasn't loved by him,” Mrs. Skinner gravely replied.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0011 }

Nell’s eyes widened as she gazed toward Mrs. Skinner. Yet no trace of amusement could be seen upon that woman's features. Clearly, Mrs. Skinner found no humor in her personal situation.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0012 }

“For three years he had been a widower, with his sister running his household. After she wed, he simply desired a person to manage his residence. You ought to keep in mind that it was a place truly worth caring for. The dwelling is quite splendid. Move along, black mare. On the other hand, Thomas lacked money, and if his dwelling failed to leak during dry spells that was nearly the only good thing to mention, even if it appears somewhat picturesque. You see, however, my love belonged to Thomas, while I had no regard whatsoever for W.O. Consequently, I debated the matter internally. ‘Sarah Crowe,’ say I—Crowe was my maiden name—‘you are able to wed your wealthy suitor if you wish, yet happiness will elude you. People are unable to endure life together in this world lacking a small amount of affection. Your best course is simply to unite with Thomas, because his love is yours, your love is his, and no other outcome will suffice.’ Move along, black mare. Therefore, I informed Thomas that I would accept his proposal. Throughout my period of preparation, I refrained from ever driving by W.O.’s home because I was afraid that seeing his grand residence would plunge me into hesitation once more. At present, though, it never crosses my mind, and my existence with Thomas is completely comfortable and joyous. Move along, black mare.”
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0013 }

“What was William Obadiah’s reaction?” Nell asked.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0014 }

“Well, he made a little fuss. However, he is on his way to visit a lean old spinster in Millersville at present, and my belief is she will snap him up quickly. That woman will prove a superior spouse compared to his former one. W.O. had no desire to wed her originally. He merely requested her hand because his dad desired it, fully expecting her to refuse him. Yet listen here, she accepted. You can imagine what a fix that was. Keep moving, black mare. Excellent at managing a home though she was, she proved dreadfully stingy. Eighteen years passed with her wearing a single bonnet. Following that, she acquired a replacement, and upon encountering her along the way, W.O. failed to recognize her. Keep moving, black mare. It seems to me my own dodge was a close one. Had I wedded him, my wretchedness might have been as terrible as my unfortunate cousin’s, Odette Ann. Having taken a wealthy husband for whom she felt nothing, Odette Ann leads a dog's life. Upon visiting me this past week, she remarks, remarks she, “Sarah Skinner, I envy you. I’d rather live in a little hut on the side of the road with a man I was fond of than in my big house with the one I’ve got.” The spouse of Odette Ann isn't entirely terrible either, despite possessing such a stubborn streak that his fur coat stays on when ninety degrees is marked on the thermometer. Persuading him to act requires coaxing him toward the reverse behavior. Still, affection is lacking to ease the friction, making for a miserable existence. Keep moving, black mare. Down in the dip stands the residence of Thora—“Wayside,” according to her name for it. Pretty as a picture, wouldn't you say? My guess is you'll rejoice to depart from this spot, given the way those mail bags keep crowding you.”
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0015 }

“Indeed, but driving alongside you was something I truly enjoyed,” Nell remarked with sincerity.
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0016 }

“Get along now!” Mrs. Skinner uttered, feeling immensely pleased. “Just wait until Thomas hears about that. Receiving a praise always delights him tremendously. Trot along, black mare. Well, this is our stop. It is my hope that you do well at the school, miss. Behind Thora’s house, a shortcut runs through the marsh. Should you go by that path, exercise extreme caution. Getting trapped in that dark mire just once would draw you straight under, leaving no trace or word of you until judgment day, just like what happened to Adam Palmer’s cow. Trot along, black mare.”
{: #nw-v03-c30-p0017 }
